classification.difficultyReason: Infer the dimensions of a square-cornered offset boundary and combine composite areas with perimeter.

content.prompt: A path 1 metre wide is being placed around the grassed area of a garden, as shown below. What is the area of the grassed part of the garden? What is its perimeter? What will the area of the path be?

spec.description: H-shaped grass region with two 4 m wide, 3 m deep recesses; square-cornered path boundary offset by 1 m. Labels retain their source segment associations. Light blue identifies grass; dashed red distinguishes the outer path boundary.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no calculated dimensions or answers are printed.

answer.short:
Grassed area: $120\text{ m}^2$; perimeter: $62\text{ m}$; path area: $66\text{ m}^2$.

Subtract the recesses from the enclosing rectangle, then subtract the grassed area from the area inside the outer path boundary.
answer.worked:
The enclosing grass rectangle has width $8+4+4=16\text{ m}$ and height $9\text{ m}$. Each recess measures $4\text{ m}\times3\text{ m}$.

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{grass}}&=16\times9-2\times4\times3\\A_{\text{grass}}&=120\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$

Each recess adds two vertical sides of $3\text{ m}$ to the enclosing rectangle's perimeter.

$$\begin{align*}P_{\text{grass}}&=2(16+9)+4\times3\\P_{\text{grass}}&=62\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

The outer boundary fits an $18\text{ m}\times11\text{ m}$ rectangle. Its two recesses are each $4-2\times1=2\text{ m}$ wide and $3\text{ m}$ deep.

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{outer}}&=18\times11-2\times2\times3\\A_{\text{outer}}&=186\text{ m}^2\\A_{\text{path}}&=186-120\\A_{\text{path}}&=66\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$
